key_syntax: Dotted path into a JSON file named in 'files'. 'per_run' specs select list items with 'where' (exact match) and read 'key' from each.

papers.title: CAMINOS reference model, Fig. 1
papers.citation: Tahvili, Vinck and di Volo, PLoS Comput Biol 2026
papers.question: Does the E–PV–SOM AdEx network give about 35 Hz gamma, SOM after PV, PV > SOM > E and an onset above a critical p?
papers.verdict_note: Reproduced under v7 (amended after v6 R4 failed): f_pk, rates and R4. Missed: against PLoS CB (primary, Hamm 2026-10-14) the PV→SOM lag by the ref. 42 method is 6.47 ms against 8.5 ms (off, e 0.24), a finding that needs X. Library path, scored apart: P6 v2 PASS through the public API (Q1–Q5, C1). The 0.1 ms delay sensitivity gives the preprint's ≈ 7 ms
papers.summary: Gamma, the PV→SOM lag and the rate order reproduce at p = 0.07. The critical-p onset (Fig. 1E) runs in reverse with the external drive fixed at 560 sources (v6) and appears at p = 0.04 with the drive at p·NE sources (v7), an assumption the paper does not state for the sweep. At p = 0.07 the v6 and v7 runs are identical for all five seeds, so R1–R3 and R4v7 score one realization there.

criteria.estimand: mean rate per population over the kept 10 s
criteria.criterion: PV > SOM > E in every seed, mean E 1–3 Hz

criteria.value_label: smallest p where all seeds oscillate
criteria.reason: every run oscillates, p = 0.02 included; peak excess is largest at low p

criteria.claim: oscillations appear above a critical p (Fig. 1E)
criteria.estimand: as R4, with drive round(p·NE) sources

With the drive fixed at 560 sources (v6), every p oscillates; the onset needs the drive to scale with p. Shared-drive variant dropped (Hamm 2026-10-12).
P6 library path not attempted (B1).

papers.title: Predictive coding light, Fig. 3 (simple and complex cell tuning)
papers.citation: N'dri, Barbier, Teulière and Triesch, Nat Commun 2025
papers.question: Do the trained network's simple and complex cells show the paper's orientation, spatial-frequency and phase tuning?
papers.summary: Preregistrations v4 and v5 were scored and did not pass; a new protocol follows (Hamm 2026-10-13). Orientation tuning and the simple/complex phase split reproduce. v5 scores the sf curve against the digitized Fig. 3: simple cells fail (10/16 points, error 1.5 times a flat line), complex cells miss the shape guard by 0.02. Under v5, T4 (frequency doubling, C3) passes on the v4 numbers.

21 % of complex cells prefer the lowest tested sf.
The authors' tuning-curve data archive is not opened (Hamm's call).
P6 library path not attempted (B1).

papers.title: Predictive coding light, Fig. 2 (inhibitory STDP removes predictable spikes)
papers.citation: N'dri, Barbier, Teulière and Triesch, Nat Commun 2025
papers.question: Are learned inhibitory weights and spike suppression ordered by predictability?
papers.summary: Weights and suppression are ordered 1 > 2 > 3 in every network on the standalone model (P0) and on the jaxfne HDP kernel with the time-averaged weight (K0b); the end-of-epoch weight fails in 1 of 3 networks (K0). The paper's Fig. 2d values were not available, so there is no numerical comparison.
open: A scored comparison needs the paper's Fig. 2d values.

papers.title: Hodgkin–Huxley reference against a reduced jaxfne neuron (AT-01)
papers.question: How closely does a reduced jaxfne neuron follow a Hodgkin–Huxley cell under the same current step?
papers.summary: Rate agrees; peak voltage, resting voltage and first-spike time are outside the tolerances declared before the run.
open: No overall verdict is recorded.
One run; each arm fires one spike in 50 ms.

papers.title: Q-learning on jaxfne network features
papers.question: Can a linear Q-learner on network spike counts learn the optimal policy of chain5 and corridor7?
papers.summary: Network features reach and hold the corridor7 policy in 5 of 5 seeds, later than tabular (222–486 episodes against 2–23) with about a third of its Q error; the flat control never learns it.
open: Why the network code has lower Q error is untested (no ablation).

papers.title: Izhikevich 2003, Figs. 2 and 3 (single-cell patterns and the 1000-cell network)
papers.question: Does jaxfne's existing Izhikevich kernel reproduce the paper's single-cell firing patterns (Fig. 2) and the 1000-cell network rhythm (Fig. 3)?
papers.summary: Preregistration v7 was scored and did not pass. Six of eight single-cell patterns reproduce; FS adapts (ISI ratio 1.86) and the resonator spikes once. The network has the paper's rate, alpha and gamma peaks, but its firing is too regular (median ISI CV 0.40 against 0.6 to 1.5), and the float64 reference arm of net.m gives 0.39 too.

criteria.estimand: first passing I+ of the ascending search

criteria.claim: RZ: damped subthreshold oscillation, no spike

criteria.reason: too regular; the reference arm gives 0.39

open: Amendment v8.2 (post hoc, signed 2026-10-13; scores/p3_v8_score.json): Fig. 2 passes 8 of 8 with the C8 pulse at I = 2 and C4 as the least-adapting type (FS 1.86 against RS 2.53 and LTS 4.39). N2 stays a failed paper claim.

S1 (rescored on each arm's own step) moves N3 across its band edge. The net.m update-order arm (PREREG_P3b.md) stopped at its equivalence gate (v5): the JAX arm drifts from the NumPy reference faster than a one-ulp input change (RESULT_P3.md).

papers.title: GSDR, Fig. 6 (a 50-neuron E, SST-like and PV-like circuit fitted to recorded spectra)
papers.citation: Nejat, Sherfey and Bastos, PLOS One 2026
papers.question: Does GSDR fit the 50-neuron Hodgkin–Huxley circuit to the recorded spectra when the circuit and the optimizer run in jaxfne?
papers.summary: Source record drafted. A pilot fit in the lane reached a saturated regime (κ ≈ 0.95 against 0.0156 in the data); the next step is a sweep of g = J_I/J_E at fixed drive before any further fit.
open: Port spec, calibration record and the pilot fit are in the lane clone and wait for integration on dev.
The drive and J_E anchor for the g sweep are not yet recorded.

papers.title: Destexhe 2009, Fig. 6B (self-sustained asynchronous irregular state in an AdEx cortical network)
papers.question: Does the jaxfne AdEx core, at the paper's parameters, sustain the asynchronous irregular state of Fig. 6B with its rates, CV_ISI and pairwise correlation?
papers.summary: The AdEx core features the port needs are on dev (Vpeak detection threshold, external-drive schedules, capped Bernoulli sampling). The port is built in the lane clone (28 lane tests pass); its preregistration is drafted and unsigned, and scored seeds 1–8 (S2) are queued.
open: Rebase the lane onto the artifacts reorganization and integrate on dev (T-21).
Report the authors' Vpeak beside the VT + 5Δ sensitivity (Hamm 2026-10-14).

papers.title: Brunel 2000, Fig. 8 (SR, SI fast, AI and SI slow states of a sparse LIF network)
papers.question: Does the jaxfne LIF core, at the paper's parameters, reproduce the Fig. 8 rates, regularity and global frequencies of the SR, SI fast, AI and SI slow states?
papers.summary: P1 source record written from the author's copy. The lane runs on the jaxfne core only; next per rule B8 is the pilot, then signature, then fresh seeds.
open: Pilot port of the Fig. 8 network (12,500 LIF cells, fixed indegree, single delay) through the public API.
Simulation numerics (integrator, dt, duration, seeds) are unstated in the paper and need declared P2 choices.

papers.title: Potjans and Diesmann 2014 cortical microcircuit, Fig. 6 and Table 5
papers.question: Does the jaxfne core reproduce the microcircuit's spontaneous AI state: layer-specific rates, CV above 0.8 and L6-lowest synchrony?
papers.summary: P1 source record written from the open-access PMC record. Fig. 6 claims (reference rates 0.86/4.45/7.59/1.09 Hz, CV above 0.8, L5e-highest/L6-lowest synchrony) and the Table 5 connectivity map are recorded with paper pointers. No port, no run. Next per B8: small pilot, then signature, then fresh seeds.
open: Supplementary Tables 1-3 not yet machine-read; publisher supplement links unverified.
Leak reversal unstated in the paper; NEST default or authors' code must settle it.
Thalamic transient protocol and Fig. 10/11 propagation claims deferred past P1.

papers.title: Vogels et al. 2011, Fig. 4 (inhibitory STDP balancing a recurrent network) and Figs. 1-2 (single-cell detailed balance)
papers.question: Does the jaxfne core, at the authors' parameters, reproduce the inhibitory-plasticity balance: the Fig. 4 network driven to its target rate and the Figs. 1-2 single-cell detailed balance?
papers.summary: P1 source record written from the authors' ModelDB code (the MATLAB script was in the Science SOM) plus the open-access 2013 review. Coded target rho0 = 3 Hz; paper-stated realized rates/CVs stay unknown (full text paywalled). The lane runs on the jaxfne core only; next per rule B8 is the pilot, then signature, then fresh seeds.
open: Paper full text and SOM PDF unreachable; paper-stated Fig. 4 rates/CVs unknown until a legal copy is readable.
Conductance synapses vs the current-based core LIF is a P2 fidelity question.
No plastic-I-to-E rule in the core (core STDP kernel updates excitatory-presynaptic weights only).

papers.title: Mejias et al. 2016 laminar multi-area model, Figs. 2-3 and 6-7
papers.citation: Mejias, Murray, Kennedy and Wang, Sci Adv 2(11):e1601335
papers.question: Does the jaxfne core reproduce the laminar circuit's gamma/alpha rhythms, their interlaminar coupling, and the 30-area functional hierarchy from frequency-dependent Granger causality?
papers.summary: P1 source record written from the open-access PMC record. Fig. 2-3 claims (gamma ~40 Hz, alpha ~10 Hz, PAC, alpha-suppression link) and Fig. 6-7 claims (SLN-DAI correlation, functional hierarchy, laminar-input jumps) are recorded with paper pointers. No port, no run. Next per B8: small pilot, then signature, then fresh seeds.
open: Supplementary Methods PDF unreachable with this run's tools; time constants, weights, noise, delays and GC settings stay unknown.
No Wilson-Cowan rate emitter and no spectral Granger-causality estimator in the core; P2 must build or declare deviations.
Anatomy files named on core-nets.org, which served a login wall on 2026-10-19.
